label: Isometries of CAT(0) Spaces
notes: Welcome the class to printed pages 228 through 243, where a single isometry of a CAT(0) space is classified by how far it moves points. Stress that the whole theory rests on one scalar function, the displacement, and that its infimum and where it is attained decide everything that follows.

label: The Displacement Function
notes: Define the displacement function as the distance from a point to its image. Emphasize that convexity of the metric in a CAT(0) space makes this function convex along geodesics, so it has no spurious local minima. That single convexity fact is what lets us reason cleanly about where motion is smallest.

label: Translation Length
notes: Introduce translation length as the infimum of displacement over the whole space, an isometry invariant under conjugation. Warn that an infimum need not be a minimum: the question of whether it is attained, and where, is exactly what separates the three behavioural types we are about to meet.

label: Three Types of Isometry
notes: Lay out the trichotomy: elliptic isometries fix a point with zero translation length, hyperbolic ones attain a positive infimum, and parabolic ones never attain their infimum. Tell students this slide is the map for the rest of the lecture, and that semisimple simply means elliptic or hyperbolic.

label: Elliptic Isometries
notes: An elliptic isometry has a fixed point, so its translation length is zero and is attained. Connect this to the Bruhat-Tits fixed-point theorem: a group with a bounded orbit in a complete CAT(0) space fixes the circumcentre. This is the engine behind compactness arguments later in the book.

label: Hyperbolic Isometries and Axes
notes: A hyperbolic, or axial, isometry attains a positive translation length along an invariant geodesic, its axis, on which it acts as pure translation. Point out that there may be many parallel axes, and that the displacement grows convexly as you step off any axis. The axis is the geometric heart of the type.

label: Parabolic Isometries
notes: A parabolic isometry has an infimum of displacement that is never attained; the minimizing set is empty. Use the horoball picture: orbits accumulate at a single boundary point without any invariant geodesic line. Reassure students that parabolics are precisely the obstruction to semisimplicity.

label: The Min-Set
notes: Define the min-set as the points where displacement equals translation length. It is closed and convex, and the isometry maps it to itself. Stress that for an elliptic isometry the min-set is its fixed-point set, for hyperbolic it is the union of axes, and for parabolic it is empty.

label: Splitting of the Min-Set
notes: State the structure theorem: for a hyperbolic isometry the min-set splits isometrically as a product of a convex set with the real line, the line factor carrying the translation. Explain that this is why studying one axis suffices, and how the product structure feeds the flat torus theorem.

label: Semisimple vs Parabolic
notes: Contrast semisimple isometries, elliptic or hyperbolic, with parabolic ones. Note that whether an isometry is semisimple can depend on completeness and properness of the space. Mention that in proper cocompact settings every isometry of an infinite-order element of the group tends to be semisimple, which is highly desirable.

label: Commuting Isometries and Products
notes: Discuss how commuting isometries preserve each other's min-sets, so a commuting hyperbolic shares invariant axes structure. Explain that the translation length of a product is controlled by the individual lengths, and that abelian subgroups acting freely produce flats through the splitting machinery of the previous slides.

label: Synthesis and Recap
notes: Recap the displacement function, translation length, the elliptic-hyperbolic-parabolic trichotomy, the convex min-set, and its product splitting. Send students to the notebook to plot displacement profiles on a line, a tree, and a Euclidean product, confirming minima, axes, and constant-translation behaviour by direct computation.
